shape_hint: Hexagon washer head: a hex head with an integral round flange (washer) of diameter dc under it, flat top. Below it a tapping-screw thread (ST, coarse spaced thread, full length under head to near the tip) ending in a drill point (fluted self-drilling tip of diameter dp) instead of a cone point.

role_map.k_max: max head height incl. flange (= nominal)
role_map.dp_max: max diameter of the drill point (per ISO 10666)

notes: Governing standard ISO 15480 (:1999, :2019; same numbers per fasten.it) which replaced DIN 7504 K. WARNING - an older table (DIN 7504 K edition) still appears on 3 sites (itafasteners, sunthrough-industrial, degademir) with larger head heights k_max 4.25/4.45/5.45/6.45 (ST4.2/4.8/5.5/6.3), dc_max 13.2 for ST6.3 and c_min 0.9 for ST4.2; the ISO 15480 values (5 sources) were used. ST2.9 omitted only because e_min and dp_max have 2 sources; other ST2.9 values: P 1.1, c 0.4, dc 6.3, k 2.8, s 4, sheet 0.7-1.9 (>=3 sources each) if the maintainer wants a reduced-column row. ISO 15481-15483 (pan/CSK cross-recess drilling screws) NOT covered. Web search budget ran out before ST2.9/e/dp third sources could be sought. Nominal lengths (gf/ita): 9.5 13 16 19 22 25 32 38 45 50 (further 60-80 in DIN 7504 K lists); length availability per size not verified. Independence caveat: globalfastener.com and fasten.it are standards-data aggregator pages (they reproduce the ISO/DIN tables); they count as 2 of the 3-5 sources per cell. Without them only cvtcivata, wegertseder and nfgab remain (enough for dc_max, k_max, s_max, t_min/t_max, dp_max) but P, c_min and e_min would drop below 3.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched all 9 listed URLs (+ gf detail_5281) live, HTTP 200. Built matrix 5 rows x 9 cols x 10 pages (gf22321, gf5281, fasten.it 2019/2000, cvt, wegert, nfg, ita, degademir, sunthrough) and clustered. Min clusters per column: P 3, c_min 3, dc_max 5, e_min 3, k_max 5, s_max 6, dp_max 3, t_min 6, t_max 6. Dissent only from the old-DIN cluster (k_max 3.45/4.25/4.45/5.45/6.45, dc_max ST6.3 13.2, c_min ST4.2/ST4.8 0.9 vs 0.8) and degademir typo t_min ST4.2 0.7. Sanity: dc>e>s, dp<d, monotone P/dc/k/t_max, t_max>t_min.
problems: Margin is thin: P (ST3.5 only gf, fasten.it, cvt), c_min ST4.2 (gf, fasten.it, cvt vs old-cluster 0.9), e_min (gf, fasten.it, old-cluster ita) and dp_max (cvt, wegert, old-cluster) are exactly 3 clusters; two of the votes for P/c_min/e_min are the aggregator pages gf and fasten.it (they transcribe the standard; no shared layout/typos found, so counted as 2 independent clusters).

Edition split: older DIN 7504 K table (ita, degademir, sunthrough: k_max 4.25/4.45/5.45/6.45, dc_max 13.2 at ST6.3, c_min 0.9) vs ISO 15480 values used (5 clusters). OK but cvt/wegert/nfg pages are titled DIN 7504 K while printing ISO numbers.

dp_max is not tabulated in ISO 15480 itself (gf: 'function of drilling point dp is specified in ISO 10666'); values come from DIN 7504 K-style pages (cvt, wegert) and ita - header text 'dp max' is explicit in all three, so semantics OK, but the standard note should mention ISO 10666.

t_min/t_max are the producer's key names for 'Drilling range (sheet or plate thickness) from/to'; they collide with the 't' column (t min/max) of the old ita table. Rename (e.g. drill_from/drill_to) if keys must be unambiguous.
ST2.9 row correctly excluded (e_min and dp_max only 2 clusters); ST3.9 correctly excluded.
